narrative:
The Karnataka High Court recorded a total hearing rate of 36.0% on November 12, 2026, with 1,191 cases heard out of 3,309 scheduled. This performance is consistent with the 35.6% hearing rate observed on September 3, 2026, though lower than the 44.6% rate recorded on August 31, 2026. Data indicates a negligible bias gap of 0.8% between government and commoner-related matters, suggesting balanced access for both cohorts.

Performance across court halls varied significantly. Judge Shivashankar Amarannavar (Hall 22) demonstrated high throughput, with one session reaching a 96.9% hearing rate. Other notable performances included S.R. Krishna Kumar (Hall 12) at 72.3% and T.P. Vivekananda (Hall 36) at 78.4%. Conversely, halls such as Hall 2 (Ashok S. Kinagi & Vijaykumar A. Patil) and certain rosters under Jayant Banerji reported minimal or zero hearing volume for specific segments, highlighting significant variance in daily case progression.

Hearing stage conversions show that Preliminary Hearings are currently the most efficient, with a 54.8% conversion rate. In contrast, Final Hearings remain a bottleneck, with only 14.8% of 620 scheduled cases being heard, a trend consistently lower than historical markers from August and September. Orders (38.1%) and Admission (36.0%) stages account for the bulk of the court’s activity.

Case-type distribution remains dominated by Writ Petitions (WP), which accounted for 1,286 scheduled matters with a 35.1% clearance rate. Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) and Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) followed with hearing rates of 38.0% and 39.4%, respectively. Notably, Civil Revision Petitions (CRP) showed higher than average engagement, with a 66.7% hearing conversion rate across 33 scheduled matters.
